response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), ch AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS a FROM j WHERE orderbase IS NOT NULL GROUP BY orderbase), b AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS bm FROM j) SELECT AVG(ch.a) AS mean_channel_avg_rate, AVG(ch.a - b.bm) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark FROM ch CROSS JOIN b WHERE ch.a > b.bm;

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark is the average feerate over all fee records linked to an order, ignoring NULL feerate. This is a record-weighted average, not an average of the channel averages.
orders.recordvault is unique, so joining fees to orders does not duplicate fee rows.
Orders with a NULL orderbase are not treated as a channel. Their fees still count toward the benchmark but they are not a channel group.
